settingsPage.whatIsQzTrayDesc: QZ Tray is a small program that runs in the background on your POS device. It acts as a bridge between your web browser (or installed desktop app) and your network printers. Without it, the browser cannot send print data directly to LAN printers.
settingsPage.whereToInstallDesc1: Install QZ Tray on your main POS device only — the PC or tablet where you process orders and payments. This device must be connected to the same network (router/WiFi) as your printers.
settingsPage.whereToInstallDesc2: Kitchen display tablets, customer displays, and other secondary devices do not need QZ Tray installed.
settingsPage.qzScenarioMigration: Existing LAN printers (migrating from another POS)
settingsPage.qzScenarioMigrationDesc: Your printers are already on the network with assigned IP addresses. Your existing LAN cables, IP setup, and Windows printer drivers all stay unchanged — you only need to install QZ Tray on the new POS device and tell Purple POS which printer to use.
settingsPage.qzScenarioFreshDesc: Installing network printers for the first time. You will physically connect the printers to your router, find their IP addresses, then install QZ Tray and link them to Purple POS.
settingsPage.qzMigStep1Title: Check if QZ Tray is already installed (install if needed)
settingsPage.qzMigStep1Desc: Some web-based POS systems also use QZ Tray, so it may already be installed. Look at the Windows system tray (bottom-right corner near the clock). If you see the QZ Tray icon, it is already running — skip to the next step. If not, download from qz.io and install on this Windows POS (Mac and Linux are also supported). Your existing LAN cables, printer IP addresses, and Windows drivers remain unchanged.
settingsPage.qzMigStep1AlreadyInstalledH: Already installed? You can skip the download and go to the next step.
settingsPage.qzMigStep2Title: Confirm your existing printer IP addresses
settingsPage.qzMigStep2Desc: Look up the IP for each printer from your previous POS settings, the router's connected-devices list, or the printer's network status page. The standard print port is 9100 (example: 192.168.1.100:9100).
settingsPage.qzMigStep3Title: Enter printer addresses in Purple POS
settingsPage.qzMigStep3Desc: Enter the IP:Port for each printer below, or select an existing Windows-registered printer from the dropdown. Run Test Print on each printer to verify, then click Save.
settingsPage.qzFreshStep1Desc: Connect each printer to the router with a LAN cable (recommended) or via WiFi. Make sure every printer is on the same network as the POS device.
settingsPage.qzFreshStep2Desc: Print a network status page directly from the printer (refer to the printer's manual for the button combination), or open the router's connected-devices list. The standard print port is 9100.
settingsPage.qzFreshStep3Desc: In the router's DHCP settings, reserve each printer's IP so it does not change after a reboot. Skip this only if the printer manual recommends DHCP-only.
settingsPage.qzFreshStep4Title: Install QZ Tray on the POS device
settingsPage.qzFreshStep4Desc: Download from qz.io and install on your main POS device only. Available for Windows, Mac, and Linux. QZ Tray runs automatically in the system tray after installation.
settingsPage.qzFreshStep5Title: Enter printer addresses in Purple POS
settingsPage.qzFreshStep5Desc: Enter IP:Port (example: 192.168.1.100:9100) for each printer below. Run Test Print on each printer to verify, then click Save.
settingsPage.qzCommonAllowBrowserDesc: The first time Purple POS connects, QZ Tray will ask for permission. Click "Allow" or "Remember this decision" so you are not asked again.
settingsPage.qzDesktopAppNoteTitle: Works with the installed desktop app too:
settingsPage.qzDesktopAppNoteDesc: The Purple POS desktop app uses the same QZ Tray bridge as the browser. You can install Purple POS to your desktop ("Install" button in the sidebar) and printing will keep working with the same settings.
settingsPage.qzDiagramFooter: Your existing LAN cables and network setup remain unchanged. QZ Tray simply enables the browser or desktop app to send print data through the same network.
settingsPage.qzTroubleNotConnectedDesc: Make sure QZ Tray is running (check the system tray icon in the bottom-right on Windows).
settingsPage.qzTroubleTestPrintDesc: Verify the printer IP address is correct and the printer is turned on and connected to the network.
settingsPage.qzTroubleNoPrintersDesc: QZ Tray only shows printers registered in Windows. For network-only printers, type the IP:Port address manually.
